Why does Krishna dance on a giant snake? As the story goes, a serpent named Kaliya poisoned the river Yamuna. The water turned black. Fish floated up. Birds stopped singing. Even the trees by the bank dried up.

Little Krishna climbed a kadamba tree and jumped right into the poison water. His friends screamed. Kaliya wrapped his coils around him. Then Krishna grew heavier and heavier, slipped free, and leapt onto Kaliya's hoods.
And he danced. With every step, a hood bowed down. Wait, did he destroy the snake? No. Kaliya's wives begged for mercy, and Krishna let him go, to the ocean, never to return.
That's why he dances on the serpent. Not to kill, but to clean the river, and to forgive. Comment Kaliya if you knew this one.
